An AI declaration with every filing ANNEXURE I State whether or not AI was used If it was, confirm that every AI-generated citation, rule, proposition and fact was independently verified, and accept personal responsibility. Signed by the party and the representative. The 4-point citation test The case exists and was decided by the court 1 named. The citation details are right: name, court, year, 2 volume, page or paragraph. 3 The holding attributed to it is accurate. 4 The case is relevant to the point made. Read the full judgment from a non-AI source: court websites, the Gazette, certified copies, SCC Online or Manupatra. An AI citation is unverified until cross-checked. Adv. Ashwani Kumar 05 / 09

Show-cause, strike-off, Bar Council Trigger The Registrar acts on its own, or on a report by anyone using Annexure II Show-cause & hearing The filing party is asked to substantiate the citation or fact Strike-off Of the offending citation, or the entire submission if it is material Referral Agents to the disciplinary committee; advocates to the Bar Council under the Advocates Act Good-faith reports are protected; frivolous ones can be punished. Checks don't extend deadlines unless the Registrar orders it. Adv. Ashwani Kumar 07 / 09

A checklist for IP practitioners Keep a simple AI-use log for each matter, so the declaration is honest Verify every citation against the full judgment, not a summary Keep native files and metadata of every label, invoice and screenshot you file Draft affidavits and user evidence without AI Keep client documents out of public AI tools (confidentiality and DPDP) Check opponents' filings: Annexure II lets you report fake citations Adv. Ashwani Kumar 08 / 09

TA K E AWAY From courtroom warnings to written rules. Courts have been sanctioning AI-generated fake citations case by case. Now an Indian regulator is writing the rules down: disclose, verify, and keep your evidence authentic. Other tribunals are likely to follow. Adv.
